title: Our cat game uses several AI asset tools — here is what each one actually does
author: CrownedGames
selftext:
We’re Crowned Games, developing Pet The Damn Cat! The clip is captured from the full game, not a generated video.



The asset pipeline is split by job: OpenAI image generation for backgrounds, Gemini for cats, props and cosmetics, Recraft for background removal, and Riverflow for image edits. ElevenLabs is used for sound effects and music. These are generated assets assembled into the game; describing the artwork as hand-drawn would be misleading.



For this short trailer, we cut actual gameplay captures into five scenes and kept the game interface visible. The vertical version fits the landscape footage inside the frame rather than cropping away the decisions and UI. That makes the UI smaller on a phone, but avoids pretending a clean close-up is the whole game.



For people using mixed asset pipelines: would you keep that full interface in a vertical trailer, or show fewer scenes with tighter crops?
